# AuthorStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/AuthorStandards.mdx

title: Author Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing authors in Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2026-05-27
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro

import { URLS } from "@/Consts";
import {Badge, Aside} from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

*This section covers standards for author entries in the Hardcover database, including how to format author names, handle multiple contributors, and maintain author profiles.*

:::note[Author standards are context-dependent]
No single guideline will apply cleanly in every case. Authors, identities, and histories are not always well-served by rigid or purely objective data structures. 

Accordingly, these guidelines cannot account for every author, identity, or historical context. People and cultures are complex, and bibliographic data is inherently limited in its ability to capture nuance. Librarians are encouraged to apply informed judgement, centre author self-identification where known, and prioritize the least potential for harm when making decisions that fall outside strict guidance. Context matters more than standardization. 

If you’re uncertain about how best to portray an author, seek further input via the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Librarians Discord channel</a>.
:::

## Author Names & Conventions

*Use the author name field to reflect how the author currently publishes and how readers will search for them. Prioritize the author’s own presentation of their name, formatted in a way that is consistent with their publicly attributed works.*

### Personal Name Field

Use **Personal Name** only for cases where an author's full personal or legal name differs from their publishing name and the author has publicly and reliably linked that name to their publishing identity (for example, in credits, copyright or rights statements, or via self-disclosure).

- Use this field when it serves a clear cataloguing purpose (such as disambiguation).
- Leave this field blank if the author publishes exclusively under a pseudonym and their personal name is not publicly tied to their publishing identity.
- Do not infer, guess, or reveal a non-public personal name.

Do not use **Personal Name** to list a birth name that an author has changed (including after gender transition). Avoid dead-naming even if the information appears online or is publicly available. When unsure, prioritize privacy and self-identification over completeness. For more on this topic, see [Supporting Trans & Non-binary Authors](#trans--non-binary-authors).

**Notable Examples:**
- Samuel Langhorne Clemens (published as Mark Twain)
- Charles Lutwidge Dodgson (published as Lewis Carroll)
- Mary Ann Evans (published as George Eliot)
- Eric Arthur Blair (published as George Orwell)

### Aliases & Pen Names

Use **Aliases** for pen names, pseudonyms, and stage names.
- Add the pseudonym or pen name as the alias author entry.
- In the current implementation, Hardcover supports one alias per author entry.
- When an author writes under multiple names, create a separate author entry for each name and use the “Alias of” field on the alias page to link back to the primary author.

**Notable Examples:**
- Stephen King is the primary author, but he has written under the alias Richard Bachman.
- Isaac Asimov is the primary author, but he has written under the alias Paul French.
- Nora Roberts is the primary author, but she has written under the alias J.D. Robb.

### Initials & Spacing

Follow the author’s preferred formatting for initials. Use the spacing the author uses in their own materials (official website, author bio in books, publisher page).

- **Example:** J. K. Rowling (spaced initials)
- **Example:** J.R.R. Tolkien (no spaces)

#### Author page URL (slug)

When editing the author page URL, use lowercase letters and hyphens. **Do not include full stops or spaces between initials.**

- **Example:** J. K. Rowling → jk-rowling
- **Example:** J.R.R. Tolkien → jrr-tolkien

Slugs generate automatically for new authors, but you may need to update them when editing an existing profile.

### Capitalization Sensitivity

Use standard proper-noun capitalization (e.g. Truman Capote) unless the author uses deliberate, consistent alternative styling.

- Respect the author’s intentional and consistent capitalization choices across their work and official presence.
- Treat author preference as higher priority than standardization between authors.

**Notable Examples:**
- bell hooks
- adrienne maree brown
- amanda lovelace

### Non-Latin Script Names

:::note[Future localization support]
In the future, Hardcover may support multiple name fields or localized names for authors. For now, use a Latin-script version of the author’s name for consistency and searchability unless no such version exists.
:::

If an author is commonly known in English or publishing contexts by a Latin-script transliteration, use that form as the author name. For example, **Yevgeni Grishkovetz** for the Russian author Евгений Гришковец.

Always prefer the spelling used by the author or their publisher. If no clear Latin-script version appears in those sources, consult a library authority source such as VIAF or WorldCat, which aggregate international library records and provide widely used transliterations of author names.

Where appropriate, the original-script name may be included as supplemental information (for example, in parenthesis within the bio). It may also appear in the Personal Name field, but only if that field is otherwise appropriate under the Personal Name guidelines.

If the author publishes primarily in a non-Latin script and no widely recognized Latin-script version of their name can be found, ask in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Librarians Discord channel</a> before interpreting a new transliteration.

Hardcover should not maintain separate author pages for the same person solely because one version uses a Latin-script name and another uses the author’s original-script name. See guidelines for [Merging Duplicate Authors](#merge-duplicate-authors) for more details.

## Duplicates & Disambiguation

*Keep author entries distinct. Adding verified author biography information and an author photo is the best way to prevent legitimate duplicates and avoid merges of distinct author profiles.*

### Merge Duplicate Authors

Sometimes an author might have multiple entries in the database (for example, due to variant spellings or a data import). When you discover duplicate author entries, they should be merged to one canonical entry.
Keep the entry that best matches Hardcover formatting and common publishing usage.

If you find separate profiles for the same author under Latin-script and non-Latin-script names, treat these as duplicate author records. In most cases, keep the Latin-script profile as the canonical author page for consistency and searchability, then merge the duplicate non-Latin-script profile into it. For more detailed guidance on merging authors, refer to the [Merging Standards page](../mergingstandards/#merging-authors).

### Authors Sharing the Same Name

Sometimes two or more completely unrelated authors publish under the exact same name (e.g. two writers named John Williams). In these cases, do not merge the profiles. 

Instead:
- Create a distinct author page for each author.
- Fill out this page fully with image, biography, and other distinguishing information.
- Check that the author’s URL slugs are clearly distinguished
- Check that each book is linked to the correct author entry.

### Author Disambiguation

When multiple authors share the same name, add a short disambiguator so readers can distinguish between them. Disambiguators should be clear, concise, and based on the attribute most commonly associated with the author in a publishing context. Disambiguation is applied in two places:

**Disambiguation in the authors URL slug:** Author slugs must be unique; if a slug is changed to match an existing one, an error will occur. When adding a disambiguator, choose the most recognizable and appropriate identifier for that author. Examples and preferred order of disambiguation (use the first suitable option):

- Middle initial(s) when the author regularly publishes with a middle initial. E.g.,  john-h-williams 
- Common professional identifier describing what the author is best known for when widely associated with them. E.g., john-williams-composer
- Birth year when other identifiers are not available or would be unclear. E.g., john-williams-1953

**Disambiguation in the author page bio:** Add a brief note at the top of the author bio to clarify the distinction. Ideally, this should match the disambiguation used in the author slug, such as “Not to be confused with John Williams (composer).”

## Author Biography & Field Data

*Author information shapes how readers understand an author, and they are often the first thing an author will notice about their profiles. Our goal is to represent authors in a way that aligns with how they actively present themselves currently. As such, we have strict guidelines on bios and the sources used to populate them to ensure Hardcover remains respectful towards all authors.*

### Author Page Bios

Author bios should be written in a concise, neutral, and factual way. Prioritize information the author publicly uses to describe their work and identity in a professional or publishing context, such as notable works, roles, awards, and relevant background. 

Use a documentation-style tone, do not editorialize.
Stick to verifiable facts from reliable sources. (see [Sources for Author Info](#sourcing-author-info))

Avoid subjective commentary, speculation, or personal details unless the author has intentionally provided clear information in a public and professional context.

Each of these rules should be met concurrently for any and all author information added to an author’s profile, bio, or metadata.

### Bios vs Field Data

Do not include information in the bio that has a dedicated field elsewhere. This includes demographic and personal data such as self-identified gender, BIPOC status, LGBTQIA+ status, location, and birth or death dates. If something belongs in a field, add it there rather than repeating it in the bio.

### Field - Demographics

Hardcover collects optional demographic fields for authors:
- Self-identified gender
- BIPOC status
- LGBTQIA+ status

Only complete these fields when the author has clearly self-identified in a reliable public source (for example, their author’s official website, author provided bios, or a statement the author has made publicly about themselves). If the author has not explicitly and intentionally provided this information, leave these fields unspecified.

### Field - Location

Author location is an optional field that represents where the author is currently based or the location from where they have published the majority of their works. Location does not refer to nationality, ethnicity, or heritage. Author location is often unavailable, but may be added when:

- A location is listed publicly in the author’s professional bio, author, or publishing website.
- For deceased authors, the place of birth or where they spent most of their life may be listed when this information is publicly available.

### Field - Birth & Death Dates

Use the most precise and publicly available information. If exact dates are not both publicly and readily available, enter the year only in the appropriate field.

## Sourcing Author Info

*Author information should reflect how an author presents themselves in a public and professional context. When choosing sources for author-related information, prioritize accuracy, recency, and author intent. If sources conflict, or if a detail could expose private information, leave the field blank until a reliable and author-direct source is available.*

### Using Reliable Sources

Acceptable sources for author information (bios, fields, photos, and other author details) are listed below in order of authority. Prefer sources that are author-direct, current, and clearly attributable.

1. **Author’s official website or publications:** Many authors provide an “About” page, media kit, or author bio in their books, publications, or websites. These sources most reliably reflect how the author describes themselves and what they have chosen to share publicly, usually in their own words or with their approval. Author websites and official publisher-provided author pages are also often suitable for author photos.
2. **Publisher’s website:** If an author does not have a personal website, a publisher author page can be used. However, these pages can be out of date, so where possible confirm key details against a more current author-direct source.
3. **Author’s verified and active social media:** Authors sometimes share biographical details on public facing profile pages or public posts in their own voice. This can be used when author-direct sources are unavailable, if the information has been recently provided in a professional context.
4. **Bookseller or book database:** Sources such as Amazon author pages, Kobo, and similar can be used only if the above sources are not available. These sources often have short blurbs which may not be author-supplied. Important: If you use them, rewrite as needed to avoid plagiarism and avoid carrying over subjective or promotional language.

### Avoiding Unreliable Sources

Do not “fill gaps” using indirect inference. If a detail is not clearly stated by the author or a reliable source, leave it blank. This is especially important for identity, name history, demographics, and location.

- **AI-generated content (for example, ChatGPT):** We do not allow AI-written bios. Do not generate author bios or use author-related information that has clearly been generated by AI. Author profiles should be based on human-vetted verifiable sources that reflect the author’s own public presentation.
- **Wikipedia:** Do not copy-paste from Wikipedia. While it may help you to locate primary sources, these should be verified independently and Wikipedia text should not be used as the basis for a bio.
- **Competitor databases (for example Goodreads, The StoryGraph):** We aim to build Hardcover’s data from primary sources that support and respect authors and their works. Copying author information from competitor platforms can introduce erroneous or unverified details and licensing issues.

### Citing Sources

Until Hardcover supports a dedicated field for bio sources, add a short source credit in plain text at the end of the bio text in parentheses. 

**For example:** 
```
(Source: Author’s official website).
```

This lets readers know where the information has originated from, how reliable the information is, and how recently the information was published or made available. Do not use HTML or Markdown when citing sources, as it will not render correctly.

## Author Photos & Files

*Photo norms and expectations can vary across peoples and cultures (see examples of [Cultural Context for Author Photos](#cultural-context-for-author-photos)). When selecting an author photo, prioritize how the author presents themselves publicly rather than applying a single “default” standard. When unsure, choose the least intrusive option and ask other Librarians on <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Discord</a>.*

### Choosing an Author Photo

- Use a photo that reflects how the author presents themselves both professionally and publicly.
- Photographs should be of the author, not book covers or unrelated images. 
- Prefer a clear, high-quality image, ideally a professional head-shot.
- If the author provides or uses a preferred photo (for example on their official website or publisher page), use that.
- If not, use the most recent, highest-quality image from an [acceptable source](#using-reliable-sources).

### Preferred File Formats

PNG and JPEG formats work best. The image should not have any transparency to it. Uploading WebP files directly is not currently supported; however, the image will be automatically converted to a WebP file behind the scenes regardless of the file format uploaded.

### Preferred Image Size

The larger the photo the better! If you want to upload a 15mb file, go for it. We'll resize it for optimal display around the site.
Author photos on Hardcover (as of July 27, 2025) are displayed at a maximum size of 178px by 178px. Uploading images smaller than this may result in blurriness when enlarged. For best results, upload photos that are at least 300px wide and 300px high. Images do not need to be square.

### Image Quality Scores

| Pixel count | Quality score | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 - 32,999 | <Badge text="Bad Quality" variant="danger" /> | 133 x 200 |
| 33,000 - 99,999 | <Badge text="Ok Quality" variant="caution" /> | 200 x 300 |
| 100,000 + | <Badge text="Good Quality" variant="success" /> | 300 x 450 |

## Supporting Author Representation

*Librarians have an important role in ensuring that authors are represented in ways that reflect how they present themselves publicly and professionally. Supporting author representation means prioritizing the author’s own identity, language, and presentation across their profile whenever possible.*

### Cultural Context for Author Photos

In some cultural contexts, identity and representation may be closely tied to Country, community, language group, or cultural protocols. Where an author’s cultural context or community norms meaningfully affect how they present themselves publicly, prioritize the author and their community’s preferred presentation.

#### Meaningful Settings

An author may use photos taken in locations connected to their cultural identity. For example, some Māori authors use photographs taken on marae or during cultural gatherings. If an author uses such images on their official website or publisher page, prefer those over replacing them with a more generic studio portrait.

#### Cultural Identifiers

Some authors choose photos that include cultural identifiers such as traditional clothing or ceremonial items. For example, Sámi authors may appear wearing gákti (traditional clothing) in official portraits. Similarly, prefer these photos if such elements appear in author materials.

#### Cultural Protocols

In some Australian First Peoples and Indigenous communities, there may be sensitivities around displaying images of those who have passed away. When working with images from older publications or archives, exercise additional care and prioritize photos that have been explicitly approved for public use by the author’s family or community.

These examples are limited and non-exhaustive. They are intended to very briefly and simply illustrate how cultural and community contexts may influence how author information and photos are handled or displayed, and that doing so respectfully may vary between cultures and peoples.

### Trans & Non-Binary Authors

We aim to represent authors in ways that reflect their current identity, respect their privacy, and avoid harm. This includes taking extra care when handling name changes related to gender affirmation or other personal transitions. Our default approach is to support discoverability of an author’s work while avoiding the public display or searchability of a previous name (commonly referred to as a dead-name).

#### Name Changes and Dead-names

Name changes related to gender affirmation are not treated the same as pseudonyms, pen names, or former legal names. 

If an author previously published under a previous name and now uses a new one:
- Always use the author’s current, self-identified public name on their current author profile.
- Do not add a previous name to public identity fields such as Personal Name or Aliases, unless the author has explicitly requested this and the name remains part of their public identity or publishing history on their own terms.
- Do not treat the appearance of a previous name on an older edition as a reason to add that name to current profile fields, searchable metadata, or public entries.

**Note:** This guidance applies to how an author is represented on Hardcover. It does not mean that librarians should automatically revise historical edition metadata or other edition-specific details by default. Similarly, a previous name appearing on an older edition is not, on its own, a reason to surface that name elsewhere.

#### Earlier Works & Legacy Profiles

Handle earlier works and older profiles based on the author’s current public identity and, where available, their stated preference.

If an author publicly and explicitly claims earlier works published under a previous name or dead-name:
Support attribution and discoverability through the author’s current public profile.
This means that readers should be able to find the author’s works through their current author page where appropriate.

It does not mean that librarians should automatically rewrite historical edition-level credits, cover-visible names, or other edition-specific metadata.

<details>
<summary>A more detailed example of managing earlier works connected to a current author profile</summary>

If an author now publishes as John Doe and publicly claims earlier works originally published under a previous name, the current John Doe author profile should be treated as the canonical author profile. Earlier works may be connected to that profile where needed for attribution and discoverability. However, an older edition that visibly credits a previous name on its cover or title page should not be automatically edited to replace that edition-specific credit unless the author has clearly requested that this occur or Hardcover has agreed on a specific handling approach.
</details>

If an older author page exists under a previous or dead-name:
- Create or maintain an author page under the author’s current public name if one does not already exist.
- Treat the current-name profile as the canonical profile moving forward for works published under the author’s current name.
- Do not refer to the old profile or add aliases, public notes, or disambiguators that expose the previous name unless the author has explicitly asked for this to occur.
- Do not make a previous name newly visible or searchable through public-facing fields unless the author has explicitly consented to this.
- Keep backend linking (if applicable), protection requests, and discussions about how to manage dead-name pages private.

#### When to Create a New Author Page

Create a new author page when an author is now publicly publishing under a different current name and there is no existing author page that reflects that current public identity.

- Use the new author page as the author’s current canonical profile.
- Ensure the current author profile is updated, consistent, and treated as the canonical profile moving forward.
- Determine whether requesting an edit lock on the author page would prevent reintroduction of outdated or inaccurate information.

#### Locking Author Pages 

Any backend linking or discussions of protection or suppression of legacy-name pages should occur privately, not via public facing channels (i.e., in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Librarian channel on Discord</a> rather than as a book-edit request or within more general channels open to non-librarians).

If a legacy-name page needs to be more permanently hidden, locked, protected from re-edits, or otherwise reviewed, raise it in the Librarian channel for a Senior librarian to review. 

When escalating, please include the following information:
- The current author profile link
- The legacy profile link, if one exists
- Any relevant and reliable sources showing the author’s current public name or stated preference
- A short summary of the issue or request.

#### Privacy & Consent First

- Do not make assumptions about an author’s identity, name history, or personal details; do use reliable sources.
- Do not create, merge, relink, or resurface author profiles in a way that makes a dead-name newly visible or searchable, unless the author has explicitly requested this.
- Do not remove or significantly alter an author’s previous book pages by default when an author’s name or identity is altered. 
- Do not assume that historical completeness takes priority over privacy, consent, or harm reduction.

## Author Outreach

*We want authors to feel welcome on Hardcover, and Librarians are some of the best ambassadors to make that happen. Thoughtful outreach shows authors that we care about how they are represented and how they want to be represented.*

### Check Before Contact

We welcome librarians to contact authors on their own behalf, as a Hardcover librarian; however, to ensure communication remains thoughtful, respectful, and coordinated, please follow the following steps:

- Check before contacting: Review the [Contacted Authors List][ContactedAuthors] to check whether the author has been contacted by Hardcover or a librarian previously. Multiple unsolicited contact is not advised as this may feel spam-like and reflect poorly on Hardcover.
- Log intention to contact: If they have not yet been contacted, add their information to the list before contacting them by completing the [Author Outreach Form][AuthorOutreachForm] (this will automatically update the list).

### Outreach Template

Use the [Outreach Email Template][AuthorOutreachTemplate] from an author’s contact form (if available) or your own email.

By following these steps, each author gets a single, friendly introduction to Hardcover. If they respond, wonderful! If not, we've still shown care without overwhelming them.

Discussing outreach in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Librarian channel on Discord</a> is a good way to coordinate. If you’re thinking of reaching out to a notable author, it doesn’t hurt to mention it to other librarians so everyone stays in the loop.

[ContactedAuthors]: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MlaWgpBYdaLxxTwmYZxhQ0xPNqi4kZQ4J4CVPXa6Vxg/edit?gid=308756447#gid=308756447
[AuthorOutreachForm]: https://forms.gle/ewUDjfe7SV8RdaWd6
[AuthorOutreachTemplate]: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fUmholoNHE9dR45LEREXeRUk-iwrKhlYtbzjLz9sGS8/edit?usp=sharing

---

# BookStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/BookStandards.mdx

title: Book Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing books in Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2026-01-18 18:00:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
import { URLS } from "@/Consts";
import ImageComponent from "@/components/ImageComponent.astro";
import {Badge, Aside} from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

*This guide covers standards for adding and editing books, including titles, metadata, cover editions, and duplicate handling on Hardcover.*

## Adding new books

If by searching Hardcover you cannot find a specific book, there are two methods for adding one to the database: 

1. ISBN or an external ID for a supported platform.
2. Manually

These functions are available to all users of Hardcover and the results are made immediately public to everyone. If the book you’re looking for exists, but a specific Edition of it does not, use [these instructions](/librarians/standards/editionstandards/#adding-editions) instead.

### Creating a book by ISBN or External ID

This is the most straightforward and preferred method of adding a new title to Hardcover. In addition to ISBN 10/13 lookups, Hardcover supports imports from select external platforms such as Open Library, Google Books, and Goodreads.

From the [Add Book to Hardcover](https://hardcover.app/books/new) page, select the type of identifier you have available from the dropdown, paste the ID, and click “Save.” If the book is found, its details will be imported with metadata automatically prefilled. You will be redirected to the imported edition.

As a librarian, it is your responsibility to review the imported details for any discrepancies. Importing information saves a lot of time, but mistakes on one platform shouldn't persist on Hardcover. Please review an imported edition's details after creation.

<Aside type="note">
If your newly added book doesn’t immediately appear in search results, it could be due to a caching or indexing delay. If it doesn’t appear within a day or so, reach out on Discord.
</Aside>

### Creating a book manually
There will be occasions where a book has no ISBN or presence on other book platforms, making importing its details impossible. This is common with self-published or very old books predating ISBN assignment.

In these cases, from the [Add Book to Hardcover](https://hardcover.app/books/new) page, select "Title" from the "What do you know about the book?" dropdown. This will guide you through an advanced search tool to ensure that a duplicate of the book is not created.

If there are no matching results available to enrich, you will be presented with an option to manually create a book. This may appear at the end of a list of near matches, so scroll to the bottom to find a link to proceed.

Using this option creates a new edition. Please refer to that guidance for filling out the form.

## Merging Duplicates
There are many reasons a duplicate book might appear. Translations, imports, and unmapped edition creation can lead to additional copies of a single book appearing on Hardcover. Librarians can report these duplicates for merging using [this guidance](/librarians/standards/mergingstandards/#merging-books).

## Book Title
### Titles & Translations
While Edition titles for a particular book may differ, the Book-level title is the one used throughout Hardcover in search results, lists, and within user libraries. In order to maintain consistency, Hardcover uses the official English title if one exists.

In the case of a book originally published in a language other than English, use an official English Translation if available. Otherwise, the original, untranslated title may be used. Under no circumstance should an unofficially translated book title be used.

In the case where two official, regionally specific titles exist, Hardcover defers to the most widely recognized English title. That means there's no hard and fast rule. If in doubt, use the original English title or ask in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">#librarians</a> Discord channel for advice.

**Examples include:**
- **Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone** (UK) vs Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone (US)
- **The Satsuma Complex** (UK) vs The Clementine Complex (US)

### Series Names in Titles
A book published as part of a franchise may include the franchise or series name in its title. These are often published inconsistently. To maintain order on Hardcover, let's look at an example:

_Star Wars: Brotherhood_ was published as such, with other books in the Star Wars standalone series following different conventions such as _Lords of the Sith: Star Wars_ or _Bloodline (Star Wars)_. 

Hardcover's preference is to use series titles as a prefix, only where the published title includes it.

This would not apply to books like _The Fellowship of the Ring_ or _Carl's Doomsday Scenario_ where the series title may or may not be part of the book's subtitle. In these instances, it's better to appropriately assign the books to their Hardcover series, leaving the title clean.

### Subtitles
Some books titles may include subtitles, separated by a colon. Hardcover handles these by rendering the subtitle beneath the base title when the length of the title exceeds 60 characters. No additional truncation needs to be done on the user's part.

**Examples:**
- _Babel, or The Necessity of Violence: An Arcane History of the Oxford Translators’ Revolution_

## Headline
A headline is a short, catchy summary used to grab the reader's attention, convey the essence of the book, and persuade them to buy. Often, this is included at the beginning of a book description on a Publisher's website or a bookseller's listing.

**Examples:**
- "A man. His ex-girlfriend's cat. A sadistic game show unlike anything in the universe: a dungeon crawl where survival depends on killing your prey in the most entertaining way possible." - Dungeon Crawler Carl
- "A controversial tale of friendship and tragedy during the Great Depression." - Of Mice and Men
- "The bestselling author of Ilium transforms the story of the ill-fated Franklin Expedition into a devastating historical adventure that will chill you to your core." - The Terror

Hardcover supports short headlines like these supplied by the publisher. If there isn't one available, this field may remain blank. Refrain from inventing headlines or using overtly promotional copy. See the description section below for more on that.

## Description
### Sourcing Book Details
Hardcover wishes to reflect the author and publisher's intentions for their books. Accepted sources for book description are as follows, in order of authority.

1. Book jacket summary / blurb
2. Publisher / author official website
3. Library of Congress / WorldCat
4. Booksellers (Barnes & Noble, Amazon, etc)
5. Other Book Data Sources (Open Library, Google Books, etc)

Book descriptions should be constrained to a spoiler-free introduction or summary of the book.

### Supplemental Content
In addition to a publisher-supplied summary, a table of contents may be added if the book is a collection of distinct stories. This should be added beneath the book summary.

### Undesired Content 
Additional promotional information should be removed, even if it is present in the description from the most authoritative source.

**Examples of content to remove:**
- "From the author of best-selling series ____."
- Book blurb quotes from other authors.
- Excerpts from publicized reviews.
- Information about specific editions (reprints, anniversary editions, etc.)

## Cover Edition
Each book on Hardcover has four dropdown fields available for selecting the best default edition of a book. These are used in various ways throughout the platform. The most important of them is the "cover edition."

The cover edition is the edition of the book from which some key metadata is pulled for display on the book page. Most notably, image and page count. Hardcover recommends using the most recent hardback (hardcover) edition as the cover edition. If that edition is poor in quality for any reason, please take the time to update the edition to meet the [edition standards](/librarians/standards/editionstandards/).

## Literary Type
Literary type categorizes a book into fiction or non-fiction. Often, the default is set to "unknown." When adding a book, please be sure to check this field to better improve individual stat data for readers.

## Book Category
To further categorize a book, a number of book categories are available with more to come in the future. These categories often influence how books are organized on Author pages so it's important to file them correctly. Below are the categories that exist today with a description of when they should be used.

- **Book:** A standard book. If a title doesn't fall into any of the categories below, it belongs here.
- **Novella:** A book shorter than a novel, but longer than a short story. Lines are fuzzy, but usually these are between 80-160 pages.
- **Short Story:** A brief piece of prose fiction, shorter than a novella.
- **Graphic Novel:** Catch-all for comics, manga, or other predominantly illustrated narrative material.
- **Fan Fiction:** Fiction typically written in an amateur capacity, unofficially leveraging existing intellectual property.
- **Research Paper:** Scholarly literature such as scientific journals.
- **Poetry:** Either a single work or collection of poetry.
- **Collection:** A number of works, by one author or many, collected into a single volume. Different from a compilation, see below.
- **Web Novel:** Written works of literature available primarily or solely on the Internet
- **Light Novel:** A light novel is a type of popular literature novel from Japan usually classified as young adult fiction.

Proposed categories that have not yet been added include: study guides, samples, and periodicals, and textbooks

Often these categories are dictated by the publisher or author, making guesswork unnecessary. If there is any confusion about which of these to use and when, please ask in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">#librarians</a> Discord channel for advice.

## Compilation
On Hardcover, a compilation denotes multiple books published within one volume. This differs from a collection in that we construct an additional hierarchy to show which books are contained. These can be set on the book by a librarian.

We recognize that the terminology here can be confusing. Just know that setting a compilation flag will display the book in a separate tab on the author page, allowing their primary works to be shown front and center, without additional clutter.

## Series
Another hierarchy available to users of Hardcover are series. These collect related books and can be sorted by their place in the series.

After adding a series to the book by search or by creating a new one, place is determined by two fields: Place in series number and text.

- **Place in Series (number):** This dictates where in the series the book falls.
- **Place in Series (text):** This dictates what is displayed in series lozenges. Accepts numbers, dashes, and commas only.

---

# Comic Books

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/ComicStandards.mdx

title: Comic Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing comics on Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-01-07 13:00:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
banner:
    content: "🚧 Mind your step, this page is a work in progress."

*This page outlines current standards for cataloguing comic books on Hardcover, including naming patterns for issues, volumes, and collected editions.*

# Comic Books
## Book Title
### Individual Issue

`{Series} #{Num}: {Title}`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        The Sandman #1: Sleep of the Just

        Sage #50

        The Amazing Spider-Man #92
    </details>

### Trade Paperbacks (TPB / TP)

`{Series}, Vol. {num}: {Title}`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        The Sandman, Vol. 1: Preludes & Nocturnes

        Saga, Vol. 10

        The Amazing Spider-Man, Vol. 5
    </details>

### Other Collections (Hardcover, Omnibus, Book, etc)

`{Series}: {Collection Title}`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        The Sandman: Book One

        Saga: Book Three Deluxe HC

        The Amazing Spider-Man: Omnibus Vol. 1
    </details>

Issue / Volume Numbers are not added to One Shots / Standalones that do not have multiple works in the series.

Title is optional for individual issues or TPBs as not all works include them but should generally follow how the publisher lists the work. If a title is used on one book, it should be included for all books in the series.

Publication years are not added to book names unless explicitly part of the series or title from the publisher as this information in included in the series name displayed above the book.

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        The Amazing Spider-Man (2018) #92 -> The Amazing Spider-Man #92

        Abbott: 1979 -> Abbott: 1979
    </details>

# Comic Series

## Series Titles

### Issues

`{Series} ({Year})`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        Saga

        The Amazing Spider-Man (2018-2022)

        The Amazing Spider-Man (2022-)
    </details>

### Trade Paperbacks

`{Series} ({Year}) (TPBs)`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        The Sandman (TBPs)

        The Amazing Spider-Man (2012-2022) (TBP)
    </details>

### Other Collections (Hardcover, Omnibus, Book, etc)

`{Series} ({Year}) (Collection Name)`

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        Saga (Compendiums)
    </details>

The "primary" series (aka the series name with no additional qualifiers in the name and the shortest slug) is the most regularly released format of the series. For series that release in issues, the issues would be the primary series. If a series is released only in TPBs or Volumes, this would be the primary series.

Year is an optional field used to differentiate different comic runs under the same series name. Years for series names should use the full range of the series for completed runs or the first year and a hypen for ongoing runs.

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        Wonder Woman (1987-2006)

        Wonder Woman (2003-)
    </details>

Collections of works (such as TBPs for series released as issues and all other collections) should be marked as a "Compilation" with the contained issues added. The collections should be added as a "Featured" series of that format of work but not to any of the series of the books comprising the collection (E.g., The Sandman: Book Two would be added as the second item in "The Sandman (Books)" but not to "The Sandman" or "Vertigo: Winder's Edge").

---

# Editing-FAQ.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/Editing-FAQ.mdx

title: Editing FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions for editing books / editions.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-01-07 08:00:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
draft: true
banner:
    content: "🚧 Mind your step, this page is a work in progress."

import FlagButton from "@/components/FlagButton.astro";

*This page answers common editing questions about adding books, merging duplicates, and handling edition-specific issues on Hardcover.*

## General
### How do I add a book if I can't find it on Hardcover?
If you search for a book and don’t see it in the results, head over to the Add Book to Hardcover page. On there you can add a book by ISBN 10, ISBN 13 or Goodreads ID. This is the best place to start, since there’s a chance the book wasn’t showing up in search for a number of reasons (the top being that this search cache out of date, this book has recently been manually added by a user and hasn’t been approved).

If this book doesn’t have an ISBN and isn’t on Goodreads, then you can head over to the New Edition form. This will create a new Book with this as the one new edition for it. When librarians add books using this form they’ll show up for everyone right away. When guests and non-librarians add books using this form they’ll have a “user added” boolean added to that book behind the scenes that prevents it from showing up in search.

### How do I merge books?
On the book page, click the <FlagButton /> dropdown and select `Mark as Duplicate`. This will open up a modal (or an overlay on mobile) that allows you to search for and select which book the current book is a duplicate of. Select that book and click button to mark it as a duplicate.

If your access level is greater than the impact of the merge, it’ll be merged immediately. If you try to merge a popular book into another book, the merge will be sent to an admin to double check before being run. Once it’s run you’ll receive a notification.

### When combining duplicate books/series/authors, which version should you keep?
In the case of Authors, series and characters, keep the one with the canonical English name.

For books, choose the one with the most readers using it. When another reader selects that book to read, we’ll default the “edition” that reader read to be the primary edition for this book. By selecting the book with the most readers, that means the next people who read it will also be assigned the same popular edition.

### The book cover is blurry even though the cover edition has a high resolution image
Check to make sure the file is not a webp (sometimes webp files from publishers or authors are even incorrectly marked with a .jpg extension). If this is the case you can save as in any image editor to convert to a true jpg or png before uploading to hardcover.

## Editions
### An ISBN is already in use incorrectly on another edition
Remove the ISBN from the wrong book using the `Hard Reset` button, then add it to the correct edition.

### What's the difference between 'Edition Format' and 'Reading Format' when editing a book?
On the edit edition form, we ask for both of these, but only “Reading Format” is required.
Reading format has three options: `Audiobook`, `Physical Book` and `Ebook`.

`Edition Format` is a text field that is used to elaborate on this specific edition. For example: `Hardcover`, `Mass market paperback`, `Full cast audiobook`, `Kickstarter Version`, etc.

This represents that specific edition of the book, not where you accessed it from.
It’s unlikely you’d put `Kindle Edition` here,
unless this edition was originally created for Kindle and is different from other versions.

When in doubt, and in most cases, you can leave this field blank.

## Series
### Series book count numbers low or thumbnails missing from series on author/book pages
The series book count and series previews only consider books with a published date. Check to make sure that at least one edition for all books in the series has a valid published date.

## Other
### My update didn’t work? What’s going on?
If you run into a bug, or start a thread in the bugs and questions channel with as much information as possible to help reproduce the error (link to the page you were editing, what fields you changed).

---

# EditionStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/EditionStandards.mdx

title: Edition Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing editions in Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-07-27 14:00:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
banner:
    content: "🚧 Mind your step, this page is a work in progress."

import {Badge} from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

*This guide covers standards for adding and editing editions, including cover quality, identifiers, formats, and other edition-specific metadata.*

## Covers
### Preferred file type for cover images
PNG and JPEG work the best. WebP files are not currently supported. The cover shouldn't have any transparency to it. The image is converted to a WebP file before we show it regardless of what you upload.

### Preferred file size
The larger the cover the better! If you want to upload a 15mb file, go for it. We'll resize it for optimal display around the site.

The covers we show on Hardcover (as of March 22, 2024) max out at 200px wide by 300px high. Uploading images smaller than this may result in blurriness when enlarged. For best results, we recommend uploading photos that are at least 300px wide by 450px high.

### What dimensions qualify for red, yellow and green?
We show three different quality scores for covers today. This is calculated using `height x width`.

0 - 32,999: <Badge text="Bad Quality" variant="danger" /> (ex 133 x 200)

33,000 - 99,999: <Badge text="Ok Quality" variant="caution" /> (ex: 200 x 300)

100,000 +: <Badge text="Good Quality" variant="success" /> (ex: 300 x 450)

We'd like to start showing larger covers on the book page, which will require more covers in the Great Quality range.

## Contributors
### Order of Listing Edition Contributors
Add the primary authors in the same order as they appear on the cover of the book. Additional contributors (editors, illustrators, etc) can be added in any order.

### Anthologies with Multiple Authors
For works containing numerous authors, such as anthologies of short stories, all contributing authors should be listed under the author role.

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        Unbound, published by Grim Oak Press shows the Author as "Multiple" and lists the Authors and their contributed works in the description.

        In this case, all 23 of the contributing authors should be listed as an Author on the edition.
    </details>

## Publishing Information
### Publisher Name
List the name of the company that published this edition.

Authors self-publishing under their own name should be entered as "Independently Published". Small companies, including LLCs established by the author that only publish that author's works, should still have the company name listed.

Do not include commas or periods around business entity acronyms.

    <details>
        <summary>Examples:</summary>
        Julie Carobini -> Indepenently Published

        Julie Carobini, LLC -> Julie Carobini LLC

        Julie Carobini Inc. -> Julie Carobini Inc
    </details>

### Published Date
List the date of publication for the edition provided by the publisher. It is important that at least one edition of a book have a valid publishing date for proper book display in series or other places. Hardcover will automatically select the earliest publication date for display on the book.

If a specific date of publishing does not exist or cannot be found, list the date as Jan 1 of that year. If a month but not day is available, list it as the first day of that month: 1/1/year

### Page Count
One area of book metadata that's difficult to standardize is the page count. With both physical and ebook editions, there are nuances to consider. Please follow these guidelines in order of preference.

#### Physical Editions
Physical editions are the most straightforward, particularly when a copy is available to reference. Use the page count listed in the edition itself, typically found on the copyright page or the last numbered page of the book. For better reading accuracy, avoid including blank and unnumbered pages and stick to the main content of the book.

If a physical copy is not available, use the publisher-supplied page count from their website or a reliable bookseller.

Some books may include a section of pages counted by roman numerals. In the case of non-fiction these may be included in the total page count. For fiction works, these are typically excluded unless they contain substantive content.

#### Digital Editions
Ebooks don't have a single, universal concept of “pages.” This is due to variation in font size, line spacing, and screen dimensions of the devices used to read them. When referencing page numbers, always prefer metadata-backed counts over visual or device-generated ones.

This guidance follows a best-available cascade of preference, prioritizing accuracy and reader clarity.

##### 1. Print-referenced page numbers 
This is the gold standard for ebook page counts. Some ebooks include embedded page numbers that correspond to a specific print edition. If available, use this count.

**What to look for:**
- “Page numbers based on the print edition” (common on Kindle)
- Epub-embedded metadata such as:
    - `page-list`
    - `page-break`
    - Explicit references to a print ISBN.
- Page numbers that remain consistent when you adjust font size or margins.

##### 2. Publisher-supplied page numbers
Second-best is a page count provided by the publisher. If not found in the ebook metadata, we can look to the publisher's website.

A fallback is to use the page count supplied by a digital storefront such as Amazon Kindle, Apple Books, or Kobo. These are often based on the print edition but may not be as accurate.

##### 3. Synthetic page counts
Sometimes ebooks don't have embedded page numbers, in that case, there are options for deriving a page count using text-length determinations. These are not ideal, but they can be used as a last resort.

Tools like Calibre may estimate page count based on text length. If using word count as the basis of derived-page count math, use text length of 275 words per page as a standard.

---

# MangaLightNovelStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/MangaLightNovelStandards.mdx

title: Manga & Light Novel Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing manga and light novels on Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-11-13 8:30:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
import ImageComponent from "@/components/ImageComponent.astro";
import {Aside} from "@astrojs/starlight/components";

*This guide explains how to handle manga and light novel series on Hardcover, including naming conventions, numbering, and adaptation-specific edge cases.*

## Series Naming Conventions

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/manga_series_naming.png" description="Example of light novel series naming on Hardcover" />

As with [books](../bookstandards/#what-title-should-we-use-for-the-book) of any kind, we should use the official English title whenever possible with manga and light novels.

If the series is only available in Japanese (meaning there are no English editions), retain the original Japanese title using Romaji (Latin alphabet) in square brackets.

**Example:**
- 小悪魔ティーリと救世主!? [Koakuma Teeri to Kyuuseishu!?]

If the series has been translated into other languages but not English, use the same format. Use the original edition as the Book's cover edition.

If an English edition exists, use the official English title and the English edition as the Book's cover edition.

<Aside type="note">
It's recommended to rename series as a last step as there are currently known issues around Goodreads imports creating a duplicate series which would have to be merged.

If a series slug contains a year or appears unnecessarily long, it may be possible to reclaim a shorter slug reserved from past deduplication. Report these to the Hardcover team for assistance.
</Aside>

### Disambiguating Light Novels from Manga

Some series exist in both manga and light novel formats. To help users distinguish between the two, it's necessary to disambiguate.

We recommend appending either "(Manga)" or "(Light Novel)" to the series title when both formats exist. The text in parentheses should be title-cased.

**Examples:**
- Classroom of the Elite (Light Novel)
- Classroom of the Elite (Manga)

## Volume Titles and Numbering

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/manga_series_naming_2.png" description="Example of light novel series naming on Hardcover" />

Naming conventions and disambiguation may vary from publisher to publisher or across other book data platforms. Hardcover sets its own standards to maintain consistency.

For books and all editions of manga and light novels, we follow the format:

`{Series Title} ({Disambiguation}), Vol. {num}: {Subtitle}`

Again, the text in parentheses should be title-cased. If a series has no disambiguation, that part may be omitted. That is expected for series published in only one format in its original language.

**Examples:**
- My Hero Academia (Manga), Vol. 2: Rage, You Damned Nerd
- Overlord (Light Novel), Vol. 1: The Undead King

---

# MergingStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/MergingStandards.mdx

title: Merge / Split Standards
description: Standards for merging or splitting various objects on Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-08-22 14:00:00
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro

import { URLS } from "@/Consts";
import {Aside} from "@astrojs/starlight/components";
import FlagButton from "@/components/FlagButton.astro";
import ImageComponent from "@/components/ImageComponent.astro";

*This guide explains how to merge or split books, editions, authors, and series while preserving clean canonical records on Hardcover.*

## Merging Books
<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_book_flag.png" description="Flag the duplicate book" />
On the page for the book you want to merge (i.e., the duplicate), click the <FlagButton /> button and select `Flag as Duplicate` from its menu.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_book_select.png" description="Select which book to keep" />
You will be presented with a search box to select the canonical book listing (i.e., the one you want to keep). Start typing the name of the book you want to merge into and select it from the dropdown list.

Once selected, the book will be highlighted in green and you will be presented with the option of which book to keep. At this time, we recommend selecting the book with the nicer slug. `le-dame-di-grace-adieu-e-descriptionre-storie` being less desirable than `the-ladies-of-grace-adieu-and-other-stories`.

After clicking the "Keep this one" button, your merge will be submitted. In some cases, where the book's impact score is high, this will require approval from a Senior Librarian on the Hardcover team before it is finalized. In the event that it's immediately approved, the page will redirect to the new canonical book page.

## Merging Editions
<Aside type="caution">
This feature behaves a little differently from other merges. Please read the following carefully and, if there's any doubt, ask in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">#librarians</a> channel before proceeding.
</Aside>

There will be times when two editions of a book are actually the same. Typically these are editions with no IDs (ISBN, ASIN, etc.) or otherwise missing metadata that exists on another existing edition. In these cases, we can clean up by merging these editions together.

**When not to merge editions:**
- Different IDs (e.g., ISBNs, ASINs)
- Different formats (e.g., Audiobook vs. eBook)
- Different languages (e.g., English vs. Spanish)
- Different publishers (e.g., Penguin vs. HarperCollins)

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_ed_flag.png" description="Flag the duplicate edition" />
From the edition list of the book that has a duplicate edition, select the duplicate, click the <FlagButton /> button, and select `Flag as Duplicate` from its menu.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_ed_select.png" description="Select the canonical edition" />
In the modal that appears, select the canonical edition (i.e., the one you want to keep) from the dropdown list. Its selection will be confirmed by a filled-in radio button to the left of the edition details.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_ed_change.png" description="Submit the edition merge" />
It's important that the edition to be merged is the one you started from. The edition you want to keep is the one you are selecting from the list in the modal.

Once you've selected the canonical edition, scroll back up to the top of the list, taking care not to change the selection as you go. Once you're sure your selection is correct, click the red button.

## Splitting Editions
<Aside type="caution">
This feature is currently granted on an individual basis to experienced librarians. If you do not have access to this feature, you can either report offending edition using the "Report a problem" button or post in the <a href={URLS.LIBRARIAN_DISCORD} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">#librarians</a> channel for assistance.
</Aside>

There will be times when a title has been added as an edition to the wrong book. To fix this, we can split the edition out, either into an existing book or a new one.

<Aside type="note">
It's important to check the mappings on editions before splitting them. If the edition has mappings that belong to another book, such as the one it's been mistakenly assigned to, these will need to be removed before the split. The consequence is moving reads and reviews to the incorrect book, even if the moved edition's metadata is correct.
</Aside>

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/split_ed_list.png" description="Edit the edition that doesn't belong" />
From the edition list of the book that has the incorrect edition, select the edition you want to split out and click the <FlagButton /> button to open its menu. Click `Edit this edition`.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/split_ed_change.png" description="Edit the edition that doesn't belong" />
In the book box on the edition edit page, click the "Change?" button. This will open a search box where you can search for the correct book to move the edition to. If the correct book does not exist, you can create a new one by clicking the "No book exists. Create a new book" option at the top of the dropdown list.

This will move the edition and all of its associated data (like covers, ISBNs, readers, etc.) to its new destination.

## Merging Authors
<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_author_flag.png" description="Flag the duplicate author" />
On the page for the author you want to merge (i.e., the duplicate), click the <FlagButton /> button and select `Flag as duplicate` from its menu.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_author_select.png" description="Select which author to keep" />
You will be presented with a search box to select the canonical author listing (i.e., the one you want to keep). Start typing the name of the author you want to merge into and select them from the dropdown list.

Once selected, the author will be highlighted in green and you will be presented with the option of which author to keep. At this time, we recommend selecting the author with the nicer slug. `clarke-susanna-453d6bb8-3374-4d57-9d78-0135780dd030` being less desirable than `susanna-clarke`.

After clicking the "Keep this one" button, your merge will be submitted. In many cases, where the author's impact score is high, this will require approval from a Senior Librarian on the Hardcover team before it is finalized. In the event that it's immediately approved, the page will redirect to the new canonical author page.

## Merging Series
<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_series_flag.png" description="Flag the duplicate series" />
On the page for the series you want to merge (i.e., the duplicate), click the <FlagButton /> button and select `Flag as duplicate` from its menu.

<ImageComponent imagePath="/src/content/images/librarians/merging-standards/merge_series_select.png" description="Select which series to keep" />
You will be presented with a search box to select the canonical series (i.e., the one you want to keep). Start typing the name of the series you want to merge into and select it from the dropdown list.

Once selected, the series will be highlighted in green and you will be presented with the option of which one to keep. At this time, we recommend selecting the series with the nicer slug. For *Strange & Norrell*, `strange-and-norrell` would be preferable to `strange-norrell`.

After clicking the "Keep this one" button, your merge will be submitted. In many cases, where the series' impact score is high, this will require approval from a Senior Librarian on the Hardcover team before it is finalized. In the event that it's immediately approved, the page will redirect to the new canonical series page.

## Merging Publishers
<Aside type="note">
Due to some known bugs, this section is currently under review and will be updated in the future. Publisher merges are currently being held in the Senior Librarian review queue until this is resolved.
</Aside>

---

# SeriesStandards.mdx

Source: https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs/blob/main/src/content/docs/librarians/Standards/SeriesStandards.mdx

title: Series Standards
description: Standards for adding and editing series in Hardcover.
category: guide
lastUpdated: 2025-02-08 09:57:47
layout: /src/layouts/librarians.astro
banner:
    content: "🚧 Mind your step, this page is a work in progress."

*This page covers standards for naming and organizing series, including duplicate names, adaptations, and publisher collection edge cases.*

## Duplicate Series Names
For multiple series with the same name, adjust the additional series as follows:
  - Append `(Author Name)` to the series name 
  - Append `-AuthorName` to the slug

When a series has been adapted into a different format (e.g., a manga that was novelized), we create a separate series for the adaptation:
  - The source format retains the series name (e.g., `The Summer Hikaru Died`)
  - For the adaptation, append `(Format)` to the series name (e.g., `The Summer Hikaru Died (Light Novel)`
  - For the adaptation, append `-format` to the slug (e.g., `the-summer-hikaru-died-lightnovel`)

## Publisher Collections (E.g., Penguin Little Black Classics)
For publisher or other collections where only a specific edition of a book is part of the series, a Hardcover series should not be created. The book may be instead added to a list.

---

title: Community Showcase
description: Discover projects built with the Hardcover API
lastUpdated: 2025-12-31
tableOfContents: false
template: splash

import Showcase from '@/components/showcase/Showcase.astro';

Explore the amazing projects our community has built using the Hardcover API. From browser extensions to e-ink displays, see what's possible!

<Showcase />

## Add Your Project

Built something cool with the Hardcover API? We'd love to feature it!

### What It Takes to Be Featured

Featured projects appear in the carousel at the top of the page and get extra visibility. To be considered for featuring, your project should meet these criteria:

**Required:**
- **Uses the Hardcover API** - Your project should integrate with Hardcover's GraphQL API
- **Available to the community** - Must be publicly accessible, open source, or available for download (not just a personal demo or proof of concept)
- **Complete submission** - Include author name with GitHub and/or Hardcover username, working links, and appropriate categories
- **English screenshots** - Screenshots must be in English for featuring (this may change in the future)

**Recommended:**
- **Quality screenshots** - 2-4 screenshots showing your project in action, reasonable file size (under 500KB each)
- **Detailed description** - Explain what your project does, its key features, and how it uses Hardcover
- **Active maintenance** - Project should be functional and reasonably maintained

Projects without screenshots or with non-English screenshots can still be listed but won't be eligible for featuring.

### How to Submit

1. Fork the [docs repository](https://github.com/hardcoverapp/hardcover-docs)
2. Create a new file: `src/content/showcase/your-project-slug.yaml`
3. Add any screenshots to `public/showcase/your-project-slug/`
4. Open a Pull Request
5. Tag `@revelry` in the [Hardcover Discord](https://discord.gg/edGpYN8ym8) to let us know!

### Template

```yaml
name: "Your Project Name"
slug: "your-project-slug"
summary: "One-line description (under 100 characters)"
description: |
  Longer description of your project. Markdown supported.

  - Feature 1
  - Feature 2

author:
  name: "Your Name"
  github: "your-github-username"      # optional
  hardcover: "your-hardcover-username"  # optional

links:
  - label: "GitHub"
    url: "https://github.com/..."
    type: "github"
  - label: "Website"
    url: "https://..."
    type: "website"

categories:
  - "Browser Extension"  # See full list below

dateAdded: 2025-01-15  # Today's date
dateUpdated: 2025-01-15

# Optional
screenshots:
  - src: "/showcase/your-project-slug/screenshot-1.png"
    alt: "Description of screenshot"

tags:
  - "relevant"
  - "tags"

featured: false  # Set by maintainers

# Optional - GitHub stats (updated manually or by script)
stats:
  githubStars: 100
```

### Available Categories

- Browser Extension
- Mobile App
- Web App
- CLI Tool
- E-ink Display
- Home Automation
- Desktop App
- Widget
- Integration
- Automation
- Other
